newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil -Prices seen steady to softer.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil -Prices seen steady to softer.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to remain steady to lower this week as improving production may prompt traders to sell short their stocks, Manila vegetable oil traders said.
"Because of improving production, Philippine sellers who don't want to get stuck in long positions may continue short selling this week," said a senior coconut oil trader.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam increased to 22,305 tonnes as of April 21 compared with 21,765 the previous week.
But another trader in a Philippine coconut oil mill said he expected prices to remain steady at firm levels following last week's technical bounce.
Trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines Inc said the average price of coconut oil edged up to $705.75 per tonne CIF last week from the previous $702.25.
UCAP said coconut oil exports from April 1 to 23 reached 42,200 tonnes.
The Philippines' monthly exports of coconut oil were between 50,000 and 60,000 tonnes in the first quarter of the year, traders said.
Coconut oil production suffered last year due to typhoons that hit coconut growing areas. -- Dolly Aglay (63 2) 841-8936
